Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
For this narrow gate I only need to assess the top-level/global scope that `makepkg --printsrcinfo` sources. That scope consists entirely of standard metadata variable assignments: `pkgname`, `epoch`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `url`, `arch`, `license`, `depends`, `makedepends`, and the `source` array. The `source` entry points to the project's own upstream repository (`git+https://github.com/hakaishi/nobleNote.git`), which is expected for a `-git` package. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry is normal for VCS sources and does not affect this gate since no sources are downloaded or verified here.

There is no top-level command substitution, `eval`, encoded/decoded payload, or network/exfiltration code executed at source time. All potentially risky actions (the `sed` edit in `prepare()`, `qmake6`/`make` in `build()`, and file installs in `package()`) live inside functions that are only defined, not executed, during `--printsrcinfo`, so they are out of scope for this gate and will be covered in the full audit.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level scope is standard metadata only; no executable malicious code.</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for .gitignore:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard `.gitignore` file for an Arch User Repository (AUR) package. It ignores all files in the repository except for the packaging metadata files: `.gitignore`, `PKGBUILD`, and `.SRCINFO`. This is the conventional setup for AUR git repositories, where only the build recipe is tracked in version control while source artifacts are fetched during `makepkg`. There are no network requests, obfuscated commands, dangerous system operations, or supply-chain attack indicators present. The file contains no executable code and poses no security risk.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard AUR gitignore; no malicious content detected.</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Reviewed .gitignore. Status: SAFE -- Standard AUR gitignore; no malicious content detected.
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is a standard -git AUR package for nobleNote. It fetches the project's own GitHub repository, uses `qmake6`/`make` for building, and installs files into `$pkgdir` using normal `install` and `make install` commands. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` value is normal for a VCS source and is not evidence of malicious behavior.

The only source modification is a `sed` command in `prepare()` that inserts a missing QScreen include into `src/note.cpp` so the upstream build can compile. There are no network requests to unexpected hosts, no downloads executed at build time, no obfuscation, no `eval`, no base64, no credential access, and no attempts to modify unrelated system files or exfiltrate data. The package is consistent with ordinary AUR packaging.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>No malicious behavior; standard AUR packaging with benign build fix.</summary>
</security_assessment>

It declares the upstream source as the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/hakaishi/nobleNote.git), uses SKIP for sha256sums (required and normal for VCS sources), and lists typical Qt6 build/runtime dependencies. No executable code, network calls to unexpected hosts, obfuscation, or dangerous operations are present. This is ordinary packaging hygiene.
</details>
